newsitem.title: UK: "Missing" Brent Walker man found guilty - SFO.
newsitem.headline: "Missing" Brent Walker man found guilty - SFO.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said on Thursday that Donald Anderson, former finance director of film and TV company Goldcrest, had been found guilty of perverting the course of justice by a London court.
Anderson was finance director when Goldcrest was a subsidiary of leisure and entertainment group Brent Walker Plc, led then by boxer turned entrepreneur George Walker.

Anderson was paid a total 700,000 stg to cover up the creation of 19 million stg of bogus Goldcrest profits recorded in the accounts of Brent Walker through a tortuous route taking in the U.S., Switzerland and the Isle of Man.
He collected the payments in bearer bonds and cash in Geneva, including sums laundered through the Bahamas and Lichtenstein.
New Zealander Anderson, 43, fled Britain in 1992 but surrendered to British police in November 1995.

He was absent from Britain in the summer of 1994 during the trial of Walker, who was cleared of a fraud concerning the same 19 million stg of false profits, and Wilfred Aquilina, former finance director of Brent Walker, who was convicted of a false accounting charge involving 4.5 million stg.
